pages.heading: Research question and design
pages.text: The Canopy project research question is whether a shaded reading courtyard improves afternoon study comfort. This is a fictional teaching study, not real scientific evidence. The study uses a two-week crossover design. Twenty-four adult volunteers participate. Each volunteer attends one shaded session and one unshaded session. Session order is randomized.

pages.heading: Measures and schedule
pages.text: The primary outcome is self-reported study comfort on a seven-point scale. Temperature is recorded every ten minutes using the same sensor. Sessions take place from 14:00 to 16:00. The study records no names in the analysis table; each participant receives a random code. The project budget is 1200 credits.

pages.heading: Consent and limitations
pages.text: Participants may withdraw at any time without giving a reason. Raw coded observations are retained for 90 days, then deleted. The protocol does not measure exam grades or long-term learning. The sample comes from one campus, which limits generalization. Participants cannot be blinded to the presence of shade.

pages.heading: Comfort and temperature
pages.text: In this fictional teaching dataset, the shaded sessions have a mean comfort score of 5.8 out of seven. The unshaded sessions have a mean comfort score of 4.1 out of seven. The mean comfort difference is 1.7 points. Mean air temperature is 28.2 degrees Celsius in shade and 31.4 degrees Celsius without shade.

pages.heading: Attendance and interpretation
pages.text: Twenty-two participants complete both sessions. Two participants miss their second session because of scheduling conflicts. The analysis includes only the 22 complete pairs. These descriptive results suggest better comfort in shade but do not establish improved learning. No statistical significance test or confidence interval is reported.

pages.heading: Recommendations
pages.text: The findings note recommends a larger follow-up study across three campuses. Future work should measure noise, humidity, and seating quality. The team recommends testing morning sessions as well as afternoon sessions. It does not recommend a particular tree species or construction contractor.

pages.heading: Responsible source collection
pages.text: The sample library contains three original fictional documents created for Vertebra Research. They are released under CC0 for copying and adaptation. Add only PDFs you wrote, have permission to share, or obtained under a compatible license. Do not upload confidential records to a shared demo library.

pages.heading: Checking answers
pages.text: Citations use physical PDF page numbers starting at one, not page labels printed inside a document. Open each cited passage and check whether it supports the answer. A valid document ID does not prove that an answer is correct. Scanned PDFs need OCR, which is not included in the first version.

pages.heading: Demo boundaries
pages.text: The local demonstration uses word matching and verbatim source excerpts. Live mode uses embeddings, Supabase storage, and an answer model. The demo library is shared rather than separated into individual user accounts. Turning uploads off prevents new document submissions but does not make the existing library private. Use a shared access passphrase to restrict library access.
